clue.text: Fellow beginning to contemplate marriage, say, in a city?

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: the beginning of the word contemplate supplies just its opening letter
say tells us the next word is to be taken by how it is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a marriage is a union

explanation.surface: A man starting to think about getting married, somewhere in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns UNION into the sound-alike ending -UNIAN, as in the way the city's natives are named.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or resident of Manchester is found in that English city, hence the question mark on a loose definition.

clue.text: Brothers' condition for keeping son's plant

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the condition word holds the son abbreviation

parts.note: the state of being a monk (a religious brother) is monkhood

explanation.surface: A rule of a religious order lets a boy keep a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, the poisonous flowering plant with hood-shaped blooms, is also called by this name.

clue.text: Green ink originally used in books in the Northumberland area

indicators.note: in places the books-plus-ink unit within the abbreviation for the north-east

parts.note: Northumberland is in the north-east of England, abbreviated NE

indicators.note: used in says the first letter of ink goes inside the books abbreviation

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible, a set of books

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word ink

explanation.surface: Green ink was first used in manuscripts from northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in the sense of inexperienced or innocent is a synonym of unworldly and gullible.

clue.text: Inferior boxer, perhaps?

parts.note: reads as a second-rate fighter, but a boxer is also a breed of dog, and one placed beneath is the predicted loser

explanation.definitionFit: The competitor expected to lose is the lesser contender, and a boxer is a breed of hound.

clue.text: Given protection, loses key and is abused

indicators.note: loses means one letter drops out of the protected word

parts.note: given protection from heat or electricity means insulated
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone sheltered loses their key and is mistreated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abused verbally is to be offended with rude remarks.

clue.text: Godly sustenance is at hand — with lightweight filling

indicators.note: filling means one piece is stuffed inside the other

parts.note: at hand means close by, near
CT is the abbreviation for carat, a very small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Food for the gods is close by, with a light stuffing.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical myth this was the drink of the Olympian gods, alongside ambrosia.

clue.text: Courses useful to carpet-layers

definitions.meaning: a sailing boat's zigzag courses against the wind
small broad-headed nails for fixing carpet down

explanation.definitionFit: Both a ship's changes of heading into the wind and short flat-headed nails share the name.

clue.text: Most of the career of this singer

indicators.note: most of means the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong

explanation.surface: Most of the working life of a particular vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A songbird is a singer, and this speckled bird is famed for its song.

clue.text: Business-like act involved a parrot

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: involved means twisted or entangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A professional-seeming performance featured a talking bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen joins 'Business-like' only in the surface: CO stands alone, and 'involved' scrambles the next two words into CKATIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A small crested Australian bird of the cockatoo family, popular as a pet.

clue.text: Skinheads consuming meal of braised beef, perhaps

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the outer letters swallow the meal

parts.note: the head of the word skin read as its first two letters
tea is an evening meal in Britain

explanation.surface: Shaven-headed youths eat a dinner of stewed beef.
explanation.walkthrough: TEA is the British evening meal; 'Skinheads' gives SK, the heads of 'skin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick slice of beef, sold as braising cuts, is an example of meat cooked slowly in liquid.

clue.text: A dean is drunk — it's the spirits

indicators.note: drunk means intoxicated and confused, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy cleric blamed on the alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Water nymphs of Greek myth are spirits of rivers and springs.

clue.text: Porter carrying motorists in boat

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside

parts.note: Cole Porter, the American songwriter
RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A porter carries drivers aboard a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British motorists' breakdown club; the porter is Cole Porter, not a baggage handler.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round wicker-framed craft from Wales and Ireland.

clue.text: Thin novel written by a king

parts.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A slim book by a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin fabric that can be seen through is described this way.

clue.text: Extortioner has no trouble breaking a high-flyer

indicators.note: breaking into means pushing apart and entering

parts.note: the lark soars high as it sings

indicators.note: trouble means disturb, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: An extortioner easily wrecks a successful achiever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no trouble' reads as 'finds it easy', but 'trouble' is the anagram signal working on the two words before it, giving OANSH to split the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender demanding exorbitant interest backed by threats is an extortionate usurer.

clue.text: Formerly, deliveries given a quick inspection

parts.note: formerly means once, at one time
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled

explanation.surface: Previously, parcels got a quick check.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, the 'deliveries'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid examination or appraisal, a cursory look.

clue.text: Many swear by common sense, yawning

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
to aver is to declare or swear
nous is everyday British slang for practical common sense

explanation.surface: Plenty of people trust gut sense, while stifling a yawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Yawning in the sense of a gaping wide-open hollow, like a huge cave.

clue.text: Backchat about master's uneven gait

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cheek word goes round the master abbreviation

parts.note: lip is impudent talk, backchat

explanation.surface: Cheeky talk about the boss's hobbling walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A halting walk favouring one leg.

clue.text: It's not great work, to shoot a tough old bird!

parts.note: to pot is to shoot game
a boiler is an old hen fit only for boiling

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on art, then a gleeful call to shoot a sturdy old fowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A mediocre book written quickly just to earn money.

clue.text: Equable companion occupied by the river

indicators.note: occupied by means filled by, so the companion word has the river inside

parts.note: a mate is a companion
the Oder is a river in central Europe

explanation.surface: An even-tempered friend lives by the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and even-tempered, avoiding extremes.

clue.text: Drive in a girl's motor at first reversing a lot

indicators.note: in means the reversed quantity sits inside the girl's name with its added 's

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, and 's gives IS

indicators.note: reversing tells us the word for a lot runs backwards

parts.note: many means a lot

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of motor

explanation.surface: A woman's car, initially going backwards a fair distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like motoring, matching the surface's car, but it means energy; 'reversing' turns the quantity word into YNAM, and Di's girl's name with 's is DI + IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive in the sense of energy and vigour.

clue.text: Most of the port went down quickly

indicators.note: most of means the port name loses its final letter

parts.note: Dover is the English Channel port

explanation.surface: A large part of the harbour sank fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A past tense of dive, mainly American, meaning plunged downwards.

clue.text: Student in college obtained a book with text and translations

definitions.text: a book with text and translations

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a kind of college

indicators.note: in places the learner inside the word for obtained

parts.note: got means obtained
L is a learner, a student, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A college student got hold of a bilingual edition.
explanation.definitionFit: A multilingual edition giving the same work in several languages side by side.

clue.text: Petitions provided illumination in some degree

parts.note: lit means lighted, provided light
any as an adverb means at all, to some degree

explanation.surface: Requests brought some light to the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of prayers or supplications recited in church.

clue.text: Keen to have the last word in a young officer's case

indicators.note: the officer abbreviation forms a case around the closing word of a prayer

parts.note: LT is lieutenant, a junior officer
amen is the final word of a prayer

explanation.surface: Eager to have the final say in a junior officer's legal matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief, to mourn.

clue.text: Their game caused damage to a private dwelling

indicators.note: damage means wrecking, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Their sport wrecked someone's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A secluded retreat, the home of a recluse.

clue.text: Retreat for husband, a man of the cloth

parts.note: Ven is short for Venerable, the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A peaceful refuge for a married man who is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven is a place of safety or shelter.

clue.text: On which goods may be freely examined

definitions.text: On which goods may be freely examined

parts.words: On which goods may be freely examined
parts.note: the terms under which a customer takes goods home to try before deciding to buy, often preceded by on

explanation.definitionFit: Short for approval, as in buying goods returnable if unsatisfactory.

clue.text: For mountain climbing I would use this material

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word goes upwards, read backwards

parts.note: an alp is a mountain
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: A climber's choice of fabric for the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' turns ALP to read PLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan woollen cloth, as worn in Scotland.

clue.text: Disregard note written by Sebastian's sister

indicators.note: written by places the note after the sister's name

parts.note: Viola is Sebastian's twin in Twelfth Night
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Ignore a message written by a Shakespeare heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: To breach or flout a rule is to disregard it.
